task: Interceptor as the second Light-class EnemyArchetype (plan-realizacji 4.4)

baseline.note: Reproduced from a clean tree before and after the experiment.

evidence_branch.note: Complete implementation preserved for a later retry. Not a checkpoint and not a baseline.

overflowing_segment.shared_with: the 133 B LIGHT_CODE tail that scripts/build.mjs appends to the same expanded composite

measurements.method: ld65 link of src/c/*.c with the memory area temporarily widened, reading __ENEMY_ARCHETYPE_DATA_SIZE__ and __HYBRID_C_EXT_SIZE__; the widened config was reverted and the baseline XEX re-verified.

variant_full_pursuit.description: Per-frame pursuit: the Interceptor closes on the player's column one four-HPOS cell every other frame.

variant_minimal_committed_dive.description: Cheapest credible Interceptor: commits to the player's column at admission and dives straight, no per-frame tracking. This is the measured floor, not a first draft.

growth_attribution_full_variant.note: publish_raider_profile was already reduced by replacing its three-way difficulty branch with the indexed form the Light path uses; that saving is included above.

available_legal_slack.caveat: DIRECTOR_C_LOW_RAM ($8B88 size $00F8) overlaps HYBRID_C_EXT_RAM by three bytes at $8C7D-$8C7F, so its usable tail is 3 B, not the 6 B the region size suggests. Only the 17 B tail is in the overflowing area; the other 7 B are reachable only by relocating whole C functions with #pragma code-name.
available_legal_slack.bss_note: HYBRID_LIGHT_STATE_RAM was grown from $000D to $0010 into the documented-unowned $810C-$810F window, which covered all four new C state bytes. BSS was never the constraint.

smallest_recovery_required.basis: raw added requirement minus every byte of legal slack, including the 17 B free tail of the overflowing area
smallest_recovery_required.correction_note: An earlier revision of this file reported 51/102 B and 58/109 B. Those double-counted the 17 B free tail, which is already consumed inside the 75/126 B overflow figures. The deficit-vs-area figures (75 B and 126 B) were correct; only the recovery subtraction was wrong.

recovery_candidate.current_owner: boot-only LAYOUT_D_GLUE_HOLDING buffer (src/main.s:11247), copied to its final home below $5000 by layout_d_publish_glue and unowned afterwards
recovery_candidate.why_promising: Larger than either deficit, adjacent to existing C territory ($86FA-$8700 scratch, $8701-$8775 ABI veneer), and reachable by the same startup publisher pattern already used for LIGHT_RESIDENT.
recovery_candidate.why_not_attempted: It needs a second packed transport record with its own expansion call and a startup-ordering proof that the block is written only after layout_d_publish_glue has drained the GLUE hold, inside a bootstrap prefix fixed by .assert *-start <= $01A3. That is roadmap step 4.3 (resident capacity), which this task was told not to start automatically.

architectural_findings.conclusion: The C/ASM boundary held. A third archetype needed only data, a small C behavior handler and one archetype-neutral ASM change (an indexed score lookup, size-neutral inside the fixed 17-byte BROADSIDE pad). The blocker is purely resident placement, not architecture.

cc65_finding.symptom: Indexing the archetype table with a computed offset made cc65 build a runtime pointer (sta ptr1 / lda (ptr1),y), which the build's software-stack audit rejects.
cc65_finding.rule: cc65 emits the wanted `ldy index / lda table+field,y` only when the index is a plain lvalue and the field constant is folded into the base, as in `(&enemy_archetypes.byte[field])[light_archetype_offset]`. A sum inside the subscript defeats it.
cc65_finding.applied: Difficulty-resolved reload columns are precomputed once at admission into light_post_burst_slot so the hot path keeps a plain index.

next_step: Owner decision on roadmap step 4.3 (resident capacity). Do not retry 4.4 before capacity exists.
